stem.en: Which feature should you track to see the direction of new root growth?

explanation.en: The newest root growth is at its tip.

text.en: The root tip
The colour of the water

whyWrong.en: Water colour does not show the root’s path.

text.en: The position of the label

whyWrong.en: A label identifies a drawing but does not move with the root.

stem.en: In the upright bean seedling with light from several sides, which directions did we observe?

explanation.en: The upright seedling shows a downward root and an upward shoot.

text.en: Root up and shoot down

whyWrong.en: These are the initial directions after turning the drawing upside down.

text.en: Root and shoot both down

whyWrong.en: The shoot in the upright comparison extends upward.

text.en: Root down and shoot up

stem.en: What does the shoot of C do when light enters from one side?

explanation.en: The shoot tip in C grows toward the opening.

text.en: Leans straight down like the root

whyWrong.en: Downward growth in C is shown by the root.

text.en: Bends toward the lit side as it grows
Grows away from the lit side

whyWrong.en: The bend is toward the side with the light.

stem.en: Which observation shows a response to a stimulus?

explanation.en: The shoot changes its growth direction in response to light from one side.

text.en: The shoot bends toward a light opening
The pot stays on the table

whyWrong.en: The pot’s position does not indicate a plant response.

text.en: The observer changes the drawing’s heading

whyWrong.en: A heading is written by the observer.

stem.en: What can happen to the root after an upright seedling is turned upside down?

explanation.en: The root can change its growth direction after being turned.

text.en: It keeps growing straight up

whyWrong.en: Match the later direction of the tip instead of following only the starting direction.

text.en: Its tip becomes a shoot

whyWrong.en: The same growing part remains a root.

text.en: Its new growth bends down

stem.en: Which pair compares starting position while keeping the lighting similar?

explanation.en: A and B differ in starting position and have similar lighting.

text.en: Inverted B and side-lit C

whyWrong.en: Both starting position and lighting differ in this pair.

text.en: Upright A and inverted B
Upright A and side-lit C

whyWrong.en: A and C start upright and differ in lighting.

stem.en: Which pair compares direction of light while starting both seedlings upright?

explanation.en: A has light from several sides, while C has light from one side. Both start upright.

text.en: A and C
A and B

whyWrong.en: B starts upside down and shares A’s lighting.

text.en: B and C

whyWrong.en: The starting positions differ as well as the lighting.

stem.en: Which record lets two students compare the direction of the same root on different days?

explanation.en: The dates and fixed viewpoint make the path of change easier to follow.

text.en: One undated sketch from a different viewpoint

whyWrong.en: The date and comparable viewpoint are missing.

text.en: The water levels without root sketches

whyWrong.en: Water levels are useful context but do not record the growth direction.

text.en: Labeled sketches from the same viewpoint with dates

stem.en: Why would changing both lighting and seedling starting position weaken the comparison?

explanation.en: Changing one condition at a time helps link an observed bend to that condition.

text.en: Different conditions guarantee that every plant grows the same way

whyWrong.en: Different conditions can lead to different directions of growth.

text.en: Two differences could affect how the result is interpreted
Growing tips cannot bend when two changes happen

whyWrong.en: Growing tips can bend under several conditions.

stem.en: Which statement is an observation from the sketches?

explanation.en: This sentence records a specific position visible in the later sketch.

text.en: The shoot tip in C ended closer to the opening
Directional light always makes every kind of shoot curve equally

whyWrong.en: That is an unsupported generalization about plants.

text.en: The observer expected the shoot to turn before looking

whyWrong.en: An expectation before looking is a prediction.
